name: Top Navbar
description: Persistent application header that keeps product/workspace identity, optional shell context, and account/utility context visible while page content changes. Top Navbar owns the stable header regions, fixed forward physical composition, and divider; Application Shell owns placement, Product owns Brand/Account data and behavior, and page patterns own page-specific headings and task actions.

props.name: brand
props.description: Optional product/workspace identity content for the single Brand slot. Product owns the mark, name, and any identity data.

props.name: contextLabel
props.description: Concise optional shell-context text shown between Brand and the flexible separator when showContext is true.

props.name: showContext
props.description: Controls whether the supporting shell-context label is visible. It does not change page title, navigation, or account state.

props.name: account
props.description: Optional product-owned account/utility composition for the single Account slot. Any interactive control supplied here must provide its own accessible semantics.

representations.mapsTo: fixed forward physical composition; not a public React prop
inherited Light/Dark semantic token context; no theme prop

anatomy.name: header
anatomy.description: Host-filling persistent header surface fixed at 64 CSS pixels high in the reviewed shell.

anatomy.name: brand
anatomy.description: Single Brand slot region at the physical left. Its content is optional and product-owned.

anatomy.name: context
anatomy.description: Optional concise supporting context label controlled by showContext.

anatomy.name: flexible-space
anatomy.description: Flexible separator that keeps account/utility content at the physical right as the host grows.

anatomy.name: account
anatomy.description: Single Account slot region at the physical right. Product owns account identity, appearance controls, and any interaction.

anatomy.name: bottom-divider
anatomy.description: One-pixel subtle divider along the physical bottom edge.

semantics.element: native header landmark containing product identity, optional shell context, flexible space, and product-owned account/utility content
semantics.accessibleName: The header landmark does not invent a redundant accessible label. Visible Brand, context, Account content, and any composed controls expose their own appropriate text or names.
semantics.keyboardActivation: Top Navbar adds no custom keyboard model. Only separately composed interactive controls inside Brand or Account provide native keyboard activation.
semantics.focus: Top Navbar never traps or moves focus; composed controls remain in normal document order after Brand/context content.
requirements: The root renders a native header landmark and fills the available host inline size rather than fixing the 1440px Figma example width.
The reviewed bar remains exactly 64 CSS pixels high with 24px physical inline inset, a 20px internal region gap, and a 1px semantic subtle bottom divider.
The physical composition remains fixed left-to-right: Brand, optional context, flexible space, then Account. Language direction does not reverse these shell regions.
Brand, context text, and Account content may determine their own text direction inside the fixed forward shell so Arabic text remains readable without mirroring Latin artwork.
The Figma order=forward selector has only the reviewed forward value and is not a product decision or public React prop.
Light/Dark appearance is inherited from semantic tokens. Top Navbar exposes no theme prop.
When showContext is true, contextLabel must be a non-empty string; hiding context removes only that region and does not change Brand or Account identity.
Brand and Account each accept at most one direct React child to preserve the Figma one-slot boundary. Consumers can wrap richer compositions inside that one child.
Top Navbar does not invent Northstar, account identity, avatar data, or appearance behavior when Brand or Account content is omitted.
Any actual command supplied inside Account, including an appearance control or account menu trigger, is product-owned and must provide its own accessible control name and behavior.
Application Shell owns Top Navbar placement and the content area beneath it; Top Navbar does not own breakpoints, sticky positioning, or shell routing.

Page Heading and page patterns own page title, description, and task actions. Top Navbar must not absorb Invite member, Save changes, or other page-specific actions merely because it accepts content slots.

brand.description: Single direct product/workspace identity child. Wrap multiple visual pieces inside one composition when needed.

account.description: Single direct product-owned account/utility child. Interactive controls retain their own component semantics and behavior.
